definition: Revoke means to officially cancel a right, privilege, or official document, often as a consequence or punishment.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word revoke. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know revoke should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: After the third safety violation in one month, the city moved to revoke the factory's operating permit.
Suspend is weaker than revoke: a suspended license is only paused and can come back, while a revoked license is canceled outright.
Strip is stronger than revoke: revoking takes back one specific privilege, while stripping someone of their rights takes away nearly everything at once.

Withdraw means to take back something that was granted or put forward — a company withdraws a job offer, a diplomat withdraws a proposal — and it implies no wrongdoing. Revoke is punitive and official: an authority cancels a specific right, privilege, or document as a consequence of misconduct. Anyone can withdraw for any reason; revoking answers a violation.

Cancel is the all-purpose word for officially calling off or ending something — a meeting, a subscription, an order. Revoke is narrower and harsher: an authority takes back a granted right, privilege, or official document, usually as punishment. Anything can be canceled; only something granted can be revoked, and usually for cause.

Revoke means to officially cancel a right, privilege, or official document, often as a consequence or punishment.
The state medical board gave Dr.
Hale two written warnings about falsifying patient records.
When an audit uncovered a third violation, the board finally acted: it voted to revoke his medical license.
The decision was a direct consequence of his misconduct, and it took away the one specific privilege his career depended on.
From that day forward, he could no longer legally practice medicine anywhere in the state.
The board canceled a specific professional privilege as a punishment for wrongdoing, which is precisely what revoke means.
Revoke is punitive and specific: an authority takes back a particular right, privilege, or document, usually as a consequence of wrongdoing, as in revoking a license or a visa.
Compare rescind, which is a deliberate, formal cancellation of a law, order, or agreement by a governing body rather than a punishment aimed at one holder's privilege.

For years the valley's most popular radio station promised listeners that its call-in contests were open to anyone with a phone.
Then a former producer revealed that the biggest prizes had gone, week after week, to friends of the owner reading from scripts.
The broadcasting commission held hearings, documented the rigged contests, and concluded that the station had abused the public's airwaves.
Its response was the harshest tool it had: it moved to revoke the station's broadcast license as a punishment for the deception, and the frequency went silent at midnight.
The owner may apply again in five years, the commission noted, but nothing obliges it to say yes — the license he held is gone, not resting.
